name: American Nightmare
label: Equal Vision Records
lede: Wesley Eisold roadied for Ten Yard Fight, then started a Boston band that listened to the Smiths. The band lost its name to a cease and desist and watched his words turn up on Fall Out Boy records, then got the name back and ended up suing WWE over it.

eras.title: Hardcore for people who owned Smiths records
eras.text: Boston hardcore in the late '90s ran on youth-crew positivity: In My Eyes, Floorpunch, Bane. Wesley Eisold, a Virginia Beach kid roadying for Ten Yard Fight, started a band that sounded like it had been listening to The Smiths and Joy Division instead.

years.src: Wikipedia: American Nightmare · Wikipedia: Wesley Eisold
years.h: A Ten Yard Fight roadie starts the least positive band in Boston
years.p: Wesley Eisold and Tim Cossar team up with Azy Relph and Jesse van Diest. The plan, per Wikipedia: dark and nihilistic, pointed at a scene full of positive lyrics.
years.xp:
Eisold was born in Virginia Beach in 1979, the son of a Navy officer, and was roadying for Ten Yard Fight when the band started.

He was born with one hand and has said it steered him toward electronic instruments rather than guitar or drums, which shaped what he did after American Nightmare.

years.h: A 1999 demo tape gets the band a label
years.p: The tape gets American Nightmare noticed around Boston, and the new local label Bridge 9 Records signs them.

years.h: Self-titled EP, one of Bridge 9's first records
years.p: The American Nightmare EP lands early in the catalog of the label that signed the band off its demo.

eras.title: A short album and a long tour
eras.text: Equal Vision Records put out Background Music in 2001 and American Nightmare took it on the road, including a fall run with Converge. The band also covered Black Flag.

years.cap: American Nightmare at the Rotunda, Philadelphia, May 2001
years.h: Background Music runs 23 minutes
years.p: Equal Vision catalog EVR062 comes in at 23 minutes and 33 seconds. Wikipedia lists high tempos, breakdowns, gang vocals and singalongs.

years.h: Two Bridge 9 releases and a compilation in one year
years.p: Bridge 9 puts out The Sun Isn't Getting Any Brighter, and Reflections Records collects the early EPs as Year One.

years.h: Fall 2001 on the road with Converge
years.p: American Nightmare tour North America behind Background Music with [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] on the bill.

years.cap: American Nightmare on a bigger stage, Wesley Eisold at right, c. 2002
years.h: American Nightmare take on Black Flag's Depression
years.p: The band records the song for Initial Records' Black Flag tribute Black on Black.

eras.title: Three names in a year
eras.text: A Philadelphia band called American Nightmare wanted its name, so Eisold's band tried A.N., then American Nothing, then Give Up the Ghost. It made a second album under that one and quit without warning.

years.cap: American Nightmare at The Corporation, Sheffield, England, May 3, 2003
years.src: Wikipedia: American Nightmare · Wikipedia: Background Music
years.h: A Philadelphia band wants the name back, and gets it
years.p: A Philadelphia band also called American Nightmare threatens legal action. The Boston band becomes A.N., then American Nothing, then Give Up the Ghost.
years.xp:
Kerrang reported the change in March 2003. Give Up the Ghost had been the planned title for the second album, so the album needed a new one.

Wikipedia says Background Music was reissued in 2003 under the Give Up the Ghost name.

years.h: Love American and Live in London both come from Bridge 9
years.p: The Love American EP and the live record Live in London arrive in the band's last full year.

years.h: Second album, third name
years.p: Equal Vision EVR083 has 13 songs in 31 minutes. The title Give Up the Ghost had to go once it became the band's name.

years.h: Europe is cancelled, and the band is gone a day later
years.p: In June 2004 Give Up the Ghost cancel a European tour. A day later management announces the breakup, citing health and personal reasons.

eras.title: Poetry, synths and Fall Out Boy
eras.text: Eisold started a small press and a synth project, and found his old lyrics coming back to him from one of the biggest pop-punk bands in America.

years.h: Eisold starts Heartworm Press
years.p: The small press publishes zines and books, including his poems Deathbeds (2007) and later work by Genesis P-Orridge and Boyd Rice. He also fronts the band [[Some Girls|ffee2206-eb9e-4b39-9447-8977e269ed0e]].

years.cap: Eisold on stage with Cold Cave
years.h: Eisold swaps guitars for synths and calls it Cold Cave
years.p: [[Cold Cave|f7f32d93-0801-45cb-9f5a-e68f640649f4]] begins in 2007 and goes on to records on Heartworm, Matador Records and Deathwish, including Cherish the Light Years (2011).

years.src: Wikipedia: Wesley Eisold · Wikipedia: American Nightmare
years.h: Fall Out Boy settle with Eisold over his lyrics
years.p: Accused of using his lyrics, [[Fall Out Boy|516cef4d-0718-4007-9939-f9b38af3f784]] settle out of court. Eisold gets credits on The Carpal Tunnel of Love, Golden and Bang the Doldrums from Infinity on High.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the settlement also added a credit on the multi-platinum From Under the Cork Tree (2005), where Eisold is listed as "Inspirador."

Philly.com's Dan Goss covered the dispute in 2007.

eras.title: The name comes back
eras.text: Seven years after the split the band reclaimed American Nightmare and played two shows on opposite coasts. Eisold trademarked the name in 2016, and a new album followed.

years.cap: Wesley Eisold working the crowd at an American Nightmare show
years.h: Seven years on, American Nightmare play Revere
years.p: Pitchfork announces the reunion in October: December 29, 2011 in Revere, Massachusetts, and New Year's Eve in Los Angeles. Deathwish Inc. reissues both albums.

years.h: Eisold registers American Nightmare as a trademark
years.p: The filing covers clothing, music and entertainment, for the name the band had been forced to give up.

years.cap: American Nightmare at the El Rey Theatre, Los Angeles
years.h: Togetherfest, with Youth of Today
years.p: American Nightmare tour with [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Trash Talk|3039780c-6db4-499a-8b22-ddd0bb7da0af]], Vanishing Life and Wolf Down.

years.h: After 15 years, a self-titled album on Rise
years.p: Pitchfork announced it in December 2017. The record follows We're Down Til We're Underground by 15 years.

eras.title: Anniversaries, and a wrestler
eras.text: The band kept a light schedule of shows and EPs on Deathwish. A wrestler's nickname turned into a federal lawsuit.

years.h: Cody Rhodes may use the name, with conditions
years.p: In 2019 Eisold agrees that wrestler Cody Runnels, known as Cody Rhodes, can use "American Nightmare" if his merchandise prominently shows his name. A 2021 agreement has similar terms.

years.h: Life Support lands on Deathwish
years.p: The EP is on Deathwish Inc.

years.cap: Wesley Eisold on stage in New York, c. 2022
years.h: Twenty years on, Background Music gets played front to back
years.p: American Nightmare tour the album in full.

years.h: Dedicated to the Next World is another Deathwish EP
years.p: It's out in May 2023.

years.big: "little to no reference to Runnels as a wrestler"
years.h: Eisold takes WWE to court over wrestler merch
years.p: He sues WWE, Cody Runnels and Fanatics, saying merch sold as American Nightmare broke the agreement. He wants at least $150,000.
years.xp: Per Fightful, the suit says fans turned up at the band's shows in Cody Rhodes merch and that social media tags got confused. Eisold asks for treble damages up to $300,000 for federal trademark infringement, plus attorney fees.

years.h: A 25th anniversary night in Brooklyn
years.p: The band's anniversary show in Brooklyn follows a year with no other live dates, per Wikipedia.

years.h: Tied Down Fest in Detroit
years.p: American Nightmare are on the 2025 bill.

sources.title: Wikipedia: We're Down Til We're Underground
